task.title: Enter a period
task.shortdesc: Record something that lasted for years, such as a home, by typing both dates in one box.

prereq.p: Open the page of Patrick Brontë first. shows how.

context.p: Some things last for years, such as living in one house. You can type the dates as text. This page adds the time that Patrick Brontë lived at Haworth, from 25 February 1820 to 7 June 1861.

step.cmd: Open the form for an event, as shows: choose , then , then .

stepresult.p: The day, month and year boxes give way to one box for text.

step.cmd: In the box, type from 25 February 1820 to 7 June 1861.

info.p: The box shows examples of what it reads, such as a whole date, about 1900 and between 1850 and 1860.

stepresult.p: The picture shows the box at this point. The words are typed, and the line under still says No date entered.

step.cmd: Leave the box by choosing another one, such as .

stepresult.p: The line named How the date reads fills in. It shows what the app understood.
The line for the event reads Residence, from 25 February 1820 to 7 June 1861.

result.p: The date now reads as a period, from one date to another.

postreq.p: For every kind of date, see . Next: .
